# Social Media Driving Global Demand for Hair Extensions

By [American Salon Staff](https://www.americansalon.com/person/american-salon-staff) Mar 15, 2024 1:14pm

[hair extensions](https://www.americansalon.com/keyword/hair-extensions) [extensions](https://www.americansalon.com/keyword/extensions) [social media](https://www.americansalon.com/keyword/social-media) [influencer](https://www.americansalon.com/keyword/influencer)

  ![Stylist Senada K. Ceka created this hair look with BELLAMI Hair Extensions. ](https://qtxasset.com/cdn-cgi/image/w=850,h=478,f=auto,fit=crop,g=0.5x0.5/https://qtxasset.com/quartz/qcloud2/media/image/bellami%20hair.jpg?VersionId=or7Ap18VYfW7k2_iunqOpvxNwMk2.RYC)

(BELLAMI Hair)

Fueled by aspirational posts on Instagram, Pinterest, and TikTok, sales of hair extensions and related products are booming worldwide with no sign of slowing down.

That’s according to [a new report by ResearchandMarkets.com](https://www.researchandmarkets.com/reports/5934489/hair-extension-market-global-industry?utm_source=BW&utm_medium=PressRelease&utm_code=4jgctt&utm_campaign=1943978+-+Global+Hair+Extension+Market+Analysis%2c+Size%2c+Share%2c+Growth%2c+Trends%2c+and+Forecasts+2024-2031%3a+nstagram%2c+Pinterest%2c+and+TikTok+have+Become+Influential+Catalysts+for+Growth&utm_exec=chdomspi), which surveyed 11 major extensions companies around the world to gauge their sales and forecasts.

Based on the companies’ feedback, the report predicts the market will grow by an average of 8% year over year through 2031. That would bring the global extensions market from its current $3 billion to $5 billion by the end of the decade, it says.

[

![Busy HaloCouture Extensions exhibit at IBS-NY 2024](https://qtxasset.com/quartz/qcloud2/styles/full_body_width/s3/media/image/halocouture%20extensions.jpg?VersionId=saWpd9JdueLaID.y2hi6x5i6wrVbFbnH&itok=OpEXz29l)](https://qtxasset.com/quartz/qcloud2/media/image/halocouture%20extensions.jpg?VersionId=18V.9Ug_FwXII1ZaeHMo1gBxYdBKXOqn)

HaloCouture Extensions was among the most popular exhibitors at the International Beauty Show-New York 2024 (IBS-NY )

Extensions companies surveyed were BELLAMI Hair, Godrej, Great Lengths, Klix Hair Extension, Evergreen Products Group Limited, Balmain Paris Hair Couture, Beauty Industry Group, Qingdao Organic Hair Ltd., Hair Dream, Hidden Crown, and Hair Addictionz.

The companies say they’re forming more partnerships with salons, hairstylists, and social media influencers, to capitalize on the organic interest and demand surrounding hair extensions.

They are also investing heavily in research and development to innovate and improve product quality, and to address issues related to environmental sustainability and the sale of knock-offs.

North American consumers are expected to dominate global extensions sales in the next few years, followed by Asian markets, the report says.

# The Power of Social Media for Your Hairstyling Brand

[Blog Posts](https://www.associatedhairprofessionals.com/updates/blog-posts)

If your social media strategy is subpar or even nonexistent, it’s time you take a look at the power of what social media can do for you. Social media is here to stay, and it’s time you get excited about its power of connection and business growth. Don’t be scared; we’re about to tell you exactly how to do it.

## 1\. Know your why. 

Have a purpose and set intentions for why you are getting involved. Some hair professionals have a social media presence to help reinforce the client experience they provide and show it to potential clients. Others have social media accounts to connect with other hairstylists to help reinforce their reputation. There are also platforms licensed professionals use to share their education on techniques—how-to videos, formulas, and new trends. There are also some platforms used to connect with clients and share before-and-after pics. Some questions you can also yourself to figure out your why may be:

*   What am I good at?
*   What makes me happy?
*   How do I make money?

For example, if you’re a rock star at color techniques and sharing your foil patterns and formulas is what you’re good at, then that’s a great way to start sharing your knowledge on social media.

## 2\. Share only your why. 

Most people on social media will start going down rabbit holes after some time. For example—you start a social media page sharing your awesome color techniques. People start following you because they see value in what you are sharing and why. It educates them, and they like watching what you are doing. When people start following you, they do it for the main reason of what piques their interest about you. When you start branching out and sharing topics or ideas that do not target your audience, you are likely to lose followers. Ask yourself: Who’s this for? What’s this for? If the content is speaking to the audience you want to speak to and saying what you got on social media to say (your why), share it. And share content like it. Don’t muddle your social media presence with content that doesn’t serve your why.  

## 3\. Build an audience that appreciates your why. 

Garnering a huge following of random people is pointless; they will never fulfil your why. Having a following of any size that’s your tribe (people who appreciate your why) is far more fruitful. Think about an entire stadium of strangers that came to watch a football game. They are there because they want to watch the game—not see a ballet. This is the same concept of your followers and your why. They want to see what content you share based on your why. When you have a social media community of people who appreciate your why, they become your tribe. To your tribe, your marketing can say, “People like us do things like this,” and they will understand they are the “people like us” and they will want to “do things like this,” a.k.a. the behaviors you want them to do—like booking an appointment, purchasing a product, signing up for your class, etc. Build this audience by continuously sharing only the content that supports your why, using strategic hashtags to represent the content so your tribe can find it. And don’t be afraid to reach out to your IRL (in real life) network and ask them to help share your content and cross-promote. Don’t just wait for your social network to grow. Get in there and engage, look around, comment, and make your presence known. ![women looks at iphone](/sites/associatedhairprofessionals.com/files/mstaszcuk/images/Untitled%20design%20\(61\).png)

## 4. Create a strong emotional connection to your why. 

People on social media are seeking someone they can look to for guidance, a trusted friend, or someone that they can connect with—not just a product or service. A connection must be made, and a loyalty built before you can sell or ask for anything. If your social media presence is nothing but smoke and mirrors, people will see through it. Let people get to know the real you in order to establish a true connection. Many top social media influencers will keep their website clean and professional but share insights into their life through Instagram or Facebook stories, which are temporary. That’s a story worth making a remark about, a story your clients or followers will want to share. Dig deep; you have one! Consumers can get a haircut anywhere, but what is the story behind you and yours? That is something your client will repeat and refer their friends to, especially when it coincides with the lifestyle they want to have.  

## 5\. Fulfill your why. 

You are on social media for a reason, right? Always remember your why. Don’t get caught up in the likes and follower count; that’s all for vanity. Treat it like a hobby and it will pay like a hobby. Treat it like a career and it will pay like a career. Only after you’ve established why you have a social media presence, posted only content that supports that why, attracted your tribe, and built a genuine connection with them—only then can you expect your social media following to give you business. Just as the conversation should happen in person, begin by offering what you bring to the table and clients will want to join you.

# Why the Hair Care Industry is Booming

[Home](https://www.teraxhaircare.com/)/[news](https://www.teraxhaircare.com/category/news/)/Why the Hair Care Industry is Booming

[Previous](https://www.teraxhaircare.com/2016/04/02/healthy_tricks/) [Next](https://www.teraxhaircare.com/2020/07/20/streamlining-payroll-management-in-hong-kong/)

Why the Hair Care Industry is Booming

The global hair care industry has seen impressive growth in recent years, driven by a combination of factors. Increased interest in personal grooming, the rise of social media influencers, and the growing awareness of the importance of scalp and hair health have all contributed to the expansion of this market. Consumers are now more discerning about the products they use, seeking out brands that promote natural ingredients, sustainability, and cruelty-free formulations.

In addition, hair care products are no longer just about basic maintenance; they have become a vital part of self-expression. With a wide variety of hair types, textures, and needs, consumers are looking for tailored solutions that cater to specific concerns, such as hair thinning, color treatment, and frizz control. This presents a significant opportunity for businesses to develop products that address these specific issues, while also offering unique formulations and benefits.

### Steps to Start a Hair Care Products Business

Starting a business that focuses on hair care products requires a clear vision, careful planning, and a solid understanding of your target market. Here are the key steps to consider when launching your own hair care line:

1.  **Market Research and Product Development**  
    The first step in developing hair care products is understanding the market. Identify your target audience and what their needs are. Are you creating products for people with curly hair, those seeking vegan solutions, or customers looking for high-end luxury hair care? Conducting thorough market research will help you identify gaps in the market and develop products that meet consumer demand.Once you’ve defined your target market, work with a professional chemist or formulator to create safe and effective products. Ingredients matter significantly in hair care, and offering high-quality, natural ingredients can help your products stand out from the competition.
2.  **Branding and Packaging**  
    Building a strong brand is essential in the crowded hair care market. Your brand should communicate the values and identity of your products. Whether you are promoting luxury, eco-friendly, or health-conscious products, your brand should resonate with your audience.Packaging also plays a critical role in attracting consumers. Invest in packaging that is not only visually appealing but also functional and sustainable. Sustainable packaging, such as recyclable or biodegradable containers, is increasingly popular among eco-conscious consumers.
3.  **Legal and Administrative Setup**  
    To launch your business legally, you’ll need to complete the necessary paperwork and filings. This includes registering your business name, obtaining any necessary licenses, and complying with local and federal regulations related to cosmetics. If you’re operating as a foreign entity in the United States, it’s essential to understand the legal requirements, such as acquiring a [nebraska ein for foreign entity](https://llcbuddy.com/nebraska-llc/nebraska-ein-for-foreign-entity/). This allows your business to legally operate and report taxes in Nebraska, ensuring you stay compliant with local laws.
4.  **Building a Sales and Marketing Strategy**  
    A strong marketing strategy is vital for the success of your hair care brand. Utilize social media platforms like Instagram, Facebook, and TikTok to showcase your products through engaging content and customer testimonials. Collaborating with beauty influencers and bloggers can also help spread the word about your products to a larger audience.In addition to online marketing, consider hosting events, offering free samples, and participating in trade shows to introduce your products to potential customers. Build a robust e-commerce website where customers can easily browse, learn about your products, and make purchases. To further enhance your online visibility and attract potential buyers, working with a [local SEO reseller](https://rankingslab.com/white-label-local-seo/) can help optimize your website for search engines, ensuring your brand reaches the right audience.
5.  **Distribution Channels**  
    Once your hair care products are ready to hit the market, you’ll need to establish distribution channels. You can sell your products directly through an online store or partner with retailers, both local and national. Many successful hair care brands start by selling through platforms like Amazon, Etsy, or beauty e-commerce sites before expanding into brick-and-mortar stores.You can also explore subscription-based models, where customers receive products on a regular basis. This model can help you build a loyal customer base and generate consistent revenue.

### Scaling Your Hair Care Business

Once your hair care business is up and running, it’s time to scale. This could involve expanding your product range, increasing your marketing budget, or entering new geographic markets. Offering complementary products like hair tools, styling accessories, or even educational resources on hair care can further strengthen your brand.

You may need to look into the available real estate properties in places where you want to expand your business. There are commercial spaces, warehouses and land that are available for lease or purchase. [We buy New Mexico land](https://www.landboss.net/sell-land-for-cash/new-mexico) in any condition, providing property owners with fair prices and a straightforward selling experience.

If you’re considering taking your business international, make sure to research the legal and logistical requirements of entering new markets. Establishing a presence in countries with high demand for hair care products can be a profitable move, but it requires careful planning and compliance with international regulations.

### [What Barbers, Hairstylists, and Cosmetologists Do](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/personal-care-and-service/barbers-hairstylists-and-cosmetologists.htm#tab-2)

Barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists provide haircutting, hairstyling, and other services related to personal appearance.

### [Work Environment](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/personal-care-and-service/barbers-hairstylists-and-cosmetologists.htm#tab-3)

Barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists work mostly in barbershops or salons. Most are full time, although part-time work is common. Work schedules may vary and often include evenings and weekends.

### [How to Become a Barber, Hairstylist, or Cosmetologist](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/personal-care-and-service/barbers-hairstylists-and-cosmetologists.htm#tab-4)

All states require barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists to be licensed. To qualify for a license, candidates typically must graduate from a state-approved barber or cosmetology program and pass an exam.

### [Pay](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/personal-care-and-service/barbers-hairstylists-and-cosmetologists.htm#tab-5)

The median hourly wage for barbers was $18.37 in May 2025.

The median hourly wage for hairdressers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists was $17.21 in May 2025.

### [Job Outlook](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/personal-care-and-service/barbers-hairstylists-and-cosmetologists.htm#tab-6)

Overall employment of barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists is projected to grow 7 percent from 2025 to 2035, much faster than the average for all occupations.

About 80,300 openings for barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists are projected each year, on average, over the decade. Many of those openings are expected to result from the need to replace workers who transfer to different occupations or exit the labor force, such as to retire.

## What Barbers, Hairstylists, and Cosmetologists Do[About this section](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/personal-care-and-service/barbers-hairstylists-and-cosmetologists.htm#TB_inline?height=325&width=325&inlineId=about-what-they-do)

![Image 1: Barbers, hairdressers, and cosmetologists](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/images/2711.jpg)

Hairstylists provide hair styling and beauty services.

Barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists provide haircutting, hairstyling, and other services related to personal appearance.

### Duties

Barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists typically do the following:

*   Inspect and analyze hair, scalp, and skin to recommend services or treatment
*   Discuss hairstyle options
*   Shampoo, color, lighten, and condition hair
*   Chemically change hair texture
*   Cut, dry, and style hair
*   Trim facial hair
*   Receive payments from client
*   Clean and disinfect all tools and work areas

Barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists provide hair and other services to enhance clients’ appearance. Common tools may include combs and hairbrushes, clippers and scissors, straight razors, blow dryers, and curling and flat irons. They also may keep records of products used and services provided to clients, such as hair color, hair treatment, and clipper setting.
